title: 2026-11-09-edenwave-poc-scoping-open-models

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sara Kim (Product, EdenWave), Dr. Amit Rao (Head of ML, EdenWave), Liam O'Neill (CTO, EdenWave)

[00:00] Jenna Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jenna from Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Sara Kim: Sara here.
[00:08] Dr. Amit Rao: Amit here.
[00:10] Liam O'Neill: Liam here, hello.
[00:12] Marco Alvarez: Marco from Redwood, hi.
[00:15] Jenna Park: Great, agenda — scope the POC: success criteria, workload sizing, pick an open-model shortlist, discuss benchmarks and timeline. Keep it a quick operational call.

[01:02] Sara Kim: For context, EdenWave builds customer-facing energy summaries from sensor streams, and we want LLM-generated reports in English, Spanish and Portuguese, so multilingual capability is important. Our main plan is to replace templated summaries with a more natural narrative and to surface anomalies.

[02:10] Dr. Amit Rao: Technical note — we have ~200 active concurrent users during peak hours, typical response length about 150-300 tokens, and worst-case batch of 5000 daily report generations. Latency target for UX is 2s end-to-end for a 200-token response, ideally lower. We're open to quantized models if quality is preserved.

[03:15] Marco Alvarez: Okay that gives us good constraints. Two axes: quality (domain accuracy + multilingual) and cost/latency. For open models, we typically test a few families — Llama variants, Mistral/Mixtral, Falcon, and some tuned Vicuna-style checkpoints. We should shortlist 2-3 models for the POC.

[04:00] Liam O'Neill: Are you recommending hosted or Dedicated? We care about data residency and PII from sensors — might need VPC/Private later. For POC, hosted is fine if redacted, but if we push to production we want Dedicated or Private.

[04:23] Jenna Park: Totally expected. POC can run on Redwood Hosted with a private project and log redaction. We'll include a Dedicated cost/latency estimate as part of the deliverables. Marco, can you note memory needs for Dedicated sizing?

[05:01] Marco Alvarez: Yep. For example, Llama 2 70B in 4-bit with our runtime might need a host with ~96GB HBM to get interactive perf; Mistral 8x (or Mixtral 7B variants) are much smaller and often hit good skylines for latency/cost. Falcon 40B variants can be a middle ground. There's always tradeoffs in multilingual — some models are stronger in Spanish/Portuguese than others.

[06:30] Dr. Amit Rao: On quality, our success criteria: (1) factual accuracy for measured energy values (no hallucinations on numeric readings), (2) coherent narrative in each language, (3) summarization F1/ROUGE stability on our test prompts, and (4) latency and cost must be within our SLOs. We'll provide ground-truth for ~500 documents.

[07:45] Sara Kim: And UX constraint — we don't want the first token to be delayed. Token streaming is important, so model/serving must support streaming responses.

[08:20] Marco Alvarez: Redwood runtime supports streaming and incremental KV-cache reuse for repeated prompts — that can cut latency for similar requests. Also baking in prefix caching for templated parts is possible.

[09:10] Jenna Park: Let's sketch the model shortlist. Proposed: Llama 3 family (we'll note as "LMA 3" sometimes in transcribe), Mistral Mixtral 7B / Mistral 8x, Falcon 40B, and a tuned Vicuna-style checkpoint for domain adaptation. We'll prioritize two for initial bench: one mid-size (~7-13B) and one larger (~34-70B) to compare quality vs cost. Thoughts?

[10:05] Dr. Amit Rao: I'd like the small model to be Mistral Mixtral 7B if it holds up in Portuguese. The bigger model could be Llama 3 34B if available; if not, Llama 2 70B as baseline. We want to know where quality plateaus.

[11:30] Marco Alvarez: Sounds good. For bench plan: we run three workloads — latency p95 for 200-token responses, throughput for concurrent 200 users with 150-token average, and a quality sweep on the 500 sample documents across EN/ES/PT using automatic metrics + a small human eval. We'll also run quantization tests (8-bit, 4-bit) to see memory and quality tradeoffs.

[12:45] Sara Kim: Can Redwood share a benchmark template we can run locally? We prefer one canonical config so numbers map cleanly.

[13:05] Jenna Park: Yes, we'll send a benchmark template and an instructions doc. We'll also include example infra configurations for Dedicated and recommended GPU types (A100/H100 family or equivalent depending on model size).

[14:20] Liam O'Neill: For cost modeling, can you show per-1k token costs for hosted and then a reserved instance example for Dedicated? We need to compare the break-even.

[14:38] Marco Alvarez: We'll provide rough cost curves. Often the smaller models in 4-bit on a single A100 equiv instance are cheapest per-token for medium throughput; large models are cheaper per-response at high throughput on Dedicated hardware due to batching. We'll include those charts in the doc.

[16:00] Dr. Amit Rao: On evaluation, metric suggestions? We use ROUGE for summaries but concerned about numeric accuracy. Any ideas for structured checks?

[16:20] Marco Alvarez: For numeric fidelity, easiest is to include a structured check in the prompt — ask the model to output JSON with measured values and a confidence field, then parse and compare to ground truth. We'll also include a token-level hallucination heuristic and run a small human review set.

[17:30] Sara Kim: Multilingual nuance — we need native-sounding Portuguese, not literal translations. Would the small Mistral variant require additional fine-tuning?

[17:50] Marco Alvarez: Possibly. For languages like pt-BR nuance, you might need small LoRA or instruction-tuning on 1-2k examples. For the POC we can test out-of-the-box quality; if it fails, we can propose a LoRA pass during the POC scope. That affects run-time memory by a small amount and training infra for a day or two.

[19:05] Jenna Park: Timeline proposal: Week 0 (this week) — share dataset and template; Week 1 — Redwood runs hosted bench for shortlisted models and returns numbers; Week 2 — EdenWave reviews and selects one model for a light adaptation (optional); Week 3 — final POC report and Dedicated sizing if moving forward. Does that align?

[19:45] Liam O'Neill: That's tight but doable. We want results we can demo to the board in three weeks.

[20:10] Marco Alvarez: Practical constraints — getting exact 2s p95 depends on sequence length distribution, so provide a small trace of sequences and concurrency pattern and we'll simulate. Also recommend 95th-percentile CPU + network overhead in the numbers.

[21:55] Dr. Amit Rao: Security/regulatory — for POC we want to confirm logs retention and redaction. The STO is sensitive for some customers, so we may need encryption-at-rest and KMS.

[22:20] Jenna Park: We'll attach our security overview (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS options). For Redwood Private we can hand off control plane to EdenWave's VPC. For POC hosted, we can redact and avoid sending raw IDs.

[23:50] Sara Kim: Any competitors we should watch for? We've talked to a few vendors.

[24:05] Liam O'Neill: We looked at Anthropic and some clouds (AWS Bedrock), and a smaller boutique that promised custom tuning. We want to be pragmatic: open-model path is attractive for cost and control.

[24:40] Marco Alvarez: Good note. We'll include an appendix comparing open-model cost and control vs managed models from Anthropic/OpenAI.

[25:55] Jenna Park: Back to model shortlist and immediate bench candidates: (1) Mistral Mixtral 7B (fast, cheap), (2) Llama 3 34B or Llama 2 70B (higher quality baseline), (3) Falcon 40B (middle ground). We'll run each in 8-bit and 4-bit where supported.

[27:30] Dr. Amit Rao: One more ask — can you include an evaluation for hallucination with numeric thresholds? If the model deviates by >5% on energy numbers that's a fail.

[27:45] Marco Alvarez: Yes we'll include numeric-tolerance checks in the bench harness. We'll return accuracy vs latency curves.

[29:00] Sara Kim: About instrumentation — we want Redwood Console dashboards for token-level cost, per-model latency, and per-route error tracing during the POC.

[29:15] Jenna Park: We'll provision a temporary Console workspace with dashboards and sample alerting tied to the bench. We'll show token breakdown and model traces.

[30:10] Liam O'Neill: If we go to Dedicated, what does rollout look like? Canary?

[30:20] Marco Alvarez: Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B testing and automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if the primary is unhealthy. We'll include a canary plan in the POC report.

[31:35] Dr. Amit Rao: About cost — can you provide a rough ballpark monthly for Dedicated if we commit to a 3-node pool for the larger model? Ballpark is fine.

[31:50] Marco Alvarez: Roughly, a reserved 3-node pool with A100/H100 class hardware for a 34-70B class model will be in the tens of thousands per month, but per-response cost will drop compared to hosted pay-as-you-go. We'll give specific numbers in the pricing sheet.

[33:10] Sara Kim: Let's capture the explicit success criteria for the board: 1) p95 latency <2.5s for 200-token responses on hosted bench; 2) numeric energy values deviation <5%; 3) human acceptability 4/5 on a 50-sample panel in EN/ES/PT; 4) cost estimate and Dedicated sizing completed.

[34:02] Jenna Park: I'll put those in the POC scope and we can sign off.

[35:15] Marco Alvarez: Any special infra constraints? Do you have private clouds or on-prem?

[35:25] Liam O'Neill: We run AWS in us-east-1 primarily. For Private deployment we might want a VPC peering option and HSM/KMS integration.

[35:40] Jenna Park: Noted. We'll include AWS reference architecture and KMS integration checklist.

[36:55] Sara Kim: One operational question — how do we instrument user feedback in prod? Could be a thumbs-up/down on a summary and hook that into retrain loops.

[37:10] Marco Alvarez: Yes, Redwood can emit per-request traces and metadata; you can capture that feedback and feed it back into a human-in-the-loop evaluation or for future LoRA tuning. We'll show examples.

[38:30] Dr. Amit Rao: OK, any blockers on our side? We need to prepare the 500 docs and confirm security comp.

[38:45] Sara Kim: We'll assemble the dataset and a short access doc by Thursday 2026-11-12.

[40:00] Jenna Park: Recap of next steps: we'll send benchmark template, security overview, and a cost/instance recommendation doc. We'll run initial hosted benches on the shortlisted models and return numbers within one week.

[40:25] Liam O'Neill: Sounds good. Please copy legal/security on the docs.

[41:00] Jenna Park: Will do. Any final questions?

[41:10] Sara Kim: Not from me.

[41:15] Dr. Amit Rao: None.

[41:20] Liam O'Neill: No.

[41:30] Jenna Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with the template and the scheduling link for the infra kick-off.

[44:45] Call ends.

Notes: transcript contains small transcription artifacts (model names spelled as LMA/Llama, Mixtral/Mistral variants) — common in auto transcription. The team agreed on a bench plan and shortlist.
